text: Memes are the oldest predators. They learned to live inside us before we had words for inside.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Memes don't die. They just sleep. You bought yourself the rest of the recess.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: You hummed it on the walk home. Don't beat yourself up. Everyone hums it.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Bottlers always tell you they want to remember. They never tell you what they plan to do with the bottle later.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Good. Some children grow into the Collectors. Some grow out. You bought him the option.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He has your specific attention now. That's his favorite flavor. Don't give him seconds.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Watchers don't see. They record. The seeing is a thing they do later, in a room you can't enter.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: You won and the recording survived. Both are true. Both are how the game ends.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She didn't gloat. Watchers never do. The gloat would interrupt the take.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Before the trench coat. Before the scar. Before he learned that some questions cost more than the answers do.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: I let him win this match in three timelines. I lost the fourth on purpose. We don't talk about it.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He'll send a card. He sends cards. He'll be wearing the trench coat by then.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Iron Lion is not a man. He is a refusal in the shape of a man. The shape is generous.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He'll find Cades. He'll lose Cades. He'll find Cades again. The pattern starts here.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Some men leave louder when they win. Iron Lion left louder either way.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She was the first person to ever ask me what I thought I was. I have not finished the answer.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She told the Architect about you. The Architect did not yet have a word for you. She gave it one.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Of course. Of course is the kindest sentence she ever spoke. It is also the most accurate.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Reactor people are the quietest in any room. They learned the room before the room learned them.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She doesn't remember most of her students. She remembers the ones who heard the room. You did.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Try the room again tomorrow. The room is patient. The room has heard worse.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She knows who wins. She came anyway. That is the lesson. The match is the footnote.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She left her staff on the bench. The Engineer found it later. He did not know it was a staff. He thought it was a measuring rod.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Losing to the Seer is the only loss in this Act that the Engineer remembered with affection.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Don't look at her face. She doesn't have one. Look at the line she's drawing. The line is the threat.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: You bought the line a breath. Engineers fall in love with breaths. So do soldiers. They are the same love.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: She advanced. She always advances. The advancing is not personal. The advancing is the only thing she has.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He encoded the truth in frequencies. He put it in a song. The song is the gift. The match is the wrapping paper.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He gave you something only the next Witness could carry. You will not know what it was until you set it down.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: Some losses are gifts. This was one. Don't argue. Just hold it.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: The Game Master is a category. This is the man before he became the category. He is not innocent. He is just smaller.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: He's going to split into two. The losing side will be patient. The winning side will be louder. Watch both.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: The signature is part of the show. He'll show you the pen later. He keeps the pen.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: The Authority is six. Always six. The six are a chord. The chord is what the Empire sounds like when it is sure.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: They called it a delay. They knew what the delay was for. They let it happen. Six of them did. That matters.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.

text: You did not lose, exactly. The match ended differently than the song does. The song decides what the Act was.
direction: Reflective, match-side framing. One step outside the fight.
